thread:
alex: Nighthanding — I'm primary until 08:00 PT. Mira, can you take secondary for the next 8h? I have a calendar conflict starting 02:00 PT.

mira: I can take secondary. quick note: I won't be reachable between 00:30-00:50 PT for a short meeting, leaving jamal as fallback.

jamal: noted. I'll be local primary for that 20m window. ping me if pager hits.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered 1979999988 for SERVICE_LATENCY_HIGH on inference-prod-us-west-2. Severity: P2.

elena: copying runbooks below. If KV cache spike, follow kv-cache-rollover and scale-up steps. link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-rollover

alex: Thanks. Quick coverage notes:
- primary: alex (until 08:00 PT)
- secondary: mira (full shift)
- local fallback: jamal (00:30-00:50 PT)
- outage windows: none planned

mira: Any recent flapping with model A quantized pods? I saw 3 evictions last 6h.

ops-sre: yes, we've seen a pattern when seq_len > 2048 and batch sizing spikes. Patch deployed to autoscaler yesterday but nodes still saturate under burst. Check node CPU and GPU memory.

jamal: If you need immediate mitigation, here's quick cmd to drain and restart the affected worker (restarts preserve cached KV on warm pods once they rejoin):
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon node/usw2-gpu-12
kubectl drain node/usw2-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# restart service
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime-usw2
```

alex: Good. Also remember the fast fallback model policy: route to gpt-compat-small if latency > 400ms for 3 consecutive minutes. Config here: https://console.redwood.ai/ops/routing/fallbacks

mira: For customer impact assessment: run this quick query to find affected customers (filter by route + 5xx/latency):
```
SELECT customer_id, count(*) as errors, avg(latency_ms) as avg_latency
FROM traces.requests
WHERE service = 'inference' AND region = 'us-west-2' AND timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY errors DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

elena: If we page customers, follow the customer-comms template (incidents -> customer comms). Link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/playbooks/customer-communications-template

jamal: small checklist for oncall: 
- check autoscaler logs (/var/log/autoscaler.log)
- confirm node utilization (nvidia-smi + top)
- if model kv blowup, toggle prefix cache on route (console option)
- escalate to infra if more than 2 nodes evicted in 30m

alex: I'm adding two quick runbook pointers in the thread: kv-cache-rollover, fallback-routing, node-drain. Keep this pinned.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Runbook links pinned: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-rollover, https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/fallback-routing, https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/node-drain-restart

mira: One more: if you need to temporarily reduce cost and mitigate load, enable per-route rate-limit at 3rps for non-critical customers via console. Use caution — informs billing.

elena: I'll draft a short handoff note for tomorrow ops sync: include summary of today's evictions, action taken (autoscaler patch + one node restart), and customers investigated (IDs 3412, 6550).

jamal: leaving a quick tip: when restarting runtime pods, watch /metrics for kv_cache_miss_rate. If it spikes > 15% after restart, revert and scale up instead.

alex: OK team — I'll be on my way. Mira, tag me if the pager comes back within 10 mins. Otherwise, good handoff. :thumbsup:

mira: got it. tagging jamal for the short window. thanks all.

oncall-bot: Reminder set: handoff-check-in @mira in 30m.
